With `asset: true`, it is the local file Claude uploads. A short, distinctive basename also serves as the title when nothing else gives one.

asset.description: publish with `url`: true uploads `file_path` (or each of `file_paths`) to that artifact's asset store instead of publishing it as the page — or, with `from_url` and `asset_ids` in place of `file_path`, copies those assets of another artifact into it server side (see **Calls**).

file_paths.description: publish with `asset: true` only: several local image, video, PDF, font, stylesheet or script files in place of `file_path`, up to 25 in one call, all into the artifact that `url` names; one approval covers the call, and the result lists each file's id and url, or why it was not uploaded. A CSV, Markdown, JSON or plain-text file, a symbolic or hard link, and a file outside the working directory each go in a call of their own with `file_path`.

from_url.description: publish with `asset: true`, in place of `file_path`: the SOURCE artifact's claude.ai URL — one the person can open.

asset_ids.description: publish with `asset: true` and `from_url` only: 1–10 distinct asset ids from the source artifact (from a `scope: "assets"` listing of it, or an upload result).

favicon.description: Deprecated; Claude omits it and uses `icon`.

icon.description: One short generic word for the artifact's browser-tab icon, such as chart, calendar, recipe, code or map: a plain signifier, never a product or brand name. Claude includes it on every page's first publish and omits it on a redeploy so the artifact keeps its icon, passing a new one only when the person asks. Ignored on an Artifact created from an Artifact type.

files.description: Supporting files to publish alongside the page, as a map {"published/path": "source/path" | {from, contentType} | {artifact, path, ver?} | null}. The key is what the HTML references. The source is a path on disk, or {from, contentType} when the type cannot be inferred from the published extension. An {artifact, path} source copies that Artifact's published file on the server: an Artifact the person can open, with its type carried over, never an HTML or XML document, and at most 4 source Artifact versions per publish. null removes that path on an update, and files left out are kept. A plain list publishes each file at its own spelling. Sources must be under the working directory or Claude's scratchpad directory. `preflight.js` at the artifact root is reserved: it runs against open pages when Claude publishes updates, and it must be a JavaScript module of at most 8 KiB whose default export is a function, or the publish is refused.

path.description: Path relative to the working directory (or to `root`, which may be a folder in your scratchpad directory); the file is served at this same path next to the page.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the extension for common types (css/js/json/png/…) — pass explicitly otherwise.

from.description: Source file path — relative to `root` (default: the working directory), or absolute under the working directory or your scratchpad directory.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the PUBLISHED extension for common types — pass explicitly otherwise.

artifact.description: Another artifact's claude.ai URL: the file is copied from ITS published files, server side — nothing is downloaded. You must be able to open that artifact.

path.description: The file's published path inside that Artifact, as a listing of its files prints it (not "index.html").

ver.description: A version of that Artifact to copy from instead of its current one — only versions you are served (its history, if you can edit it); omit for the current version.

edits.description: publish: small changes Claude makes to the file at `file_path` in this same call, instead of editing the file with Edit and publishing after. Use it on a page (add `url` to update an artifact from another conversation) or on one data file of an artifact made from a type (its `url`, with that file as `file_path`). Not allowed with `type_url` or `files`. Each old_str is text copied exactly from the file as it now stands and must occur in it exactly once; new_str takes its place (empty deletes it). The edits apply in order, all or none: the file is published with them and then saved with them on disk, so it stays the source for later changes; on a miss nothing is changed or published, and the result says which edit failed and why.

old_str.description: Text copied exactly from the file; must occur once.

root.description: The base directory that relative `files` sources resolve against, like a bundler root. It never changes the published path of a `files` entry. It is relative to the working directory, or absolute within it or within Claude's scratchpad directory. It requires `files`, except on an Artifact made from a type, where a data `file_path` is served at its path relative to `root`, unless a `files` map entry states its served path. Claude sends it with every such publish, set to the folder that holds the Artifact's files at their served paths.

pin.description: publish only: true also pins the published artifact to the person's claude.ai sidebar once it is published. Claude passes it only when the person asked for that. A failed pin never fails the publish, and the result says so.

limit.description: list only: the maximum number of artifacts to return (default 25).

page_token.description: list only: the `next_page_token` a listing of the same scope gave, to list the artifacts after it.

scope.description: list: which listing to return. 'mine' is the default. The others are 'shared', 'all', 'types', 'files' (with `url`) and 'assets' (with `url`, continued with `after`). See **Calls**.

type_query.description: list with scope 'types' only: limits the listing to the types whose title or description match this text best, ignoring case; a type that matches less well is left out, so a narrowed listing is not the whole catalog. Claude omits it when choosing a type for a request, unless a listing made without it says more types exist than it shows.

type.description: list only: the name of a published Artifact type, as a 'types' listing shows it (case does not matter). The listing then shows the Artifacts made from that type instead of the person's gallery. Claude passes this or `type_url`, not both.

intent.description: quickstart only (required): what is being made — 'document' (writing people will keep editing or pass around as text, such as a memo, plan, spec, proposal or notes), 'slides' (a deck or one slide), 'design' (a visual design or prototype on a canvas), 'other' (a page to look at or use: an explainer, a diagram, anything interactive, a dashboard that shows data, a spreadsheet, anything else, or unsure).

design_systems.description: quickstart only: false when a design system's link is already in hand (it is then read with its own call) or one was declined. Omitted or true, the result lists the design systems (not for a document) and, for slides or a design, attaches the default one's README.

title.description: publish: the fallback title for an HTML page whose file has no <title>. It is a name, not a summary, and Claude keeps it the same across redeploys. On a `type_url` create, it is the new Artifact's name: what the person called it, or a short descriptive name. If it is left out, the Artifact is named after the type.

description.description: publish: one sentence for the subtitle on the gallery card.

label.description: A short name for this publish, at most 60 characters (e.g. "Draft to legal"). Optional. It is a few words, not a description.

overwrite_unread.description: publish with `files` or `root` to an existing artifact: published paths this call may replace or remove although you have not read or listed them in this session. Every other path the call touches must be one you read by its `path`, saw in a file listing, or published yourself, and must not have changed since — otherwise nothing is sent and the refusal names each path. Name a path here only when the user asked for it to be replaced without looking at what is there; it never excuses a path that changed after you read it.

url.description: An existing artifact's claude.ai link (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}); a chat, project or session link is not one, and `action: "list"` lists the person's artifacts. On a publish, it is the artifact to update in place, one the person owns or was given edit access to (a read of it says "writer"). Before publishing to an artifact this conversation has neither read nor published, Claude reads it (`action: "read"`) and builds on what comes back; a publish sent without that read is refused. A refusal that hands Claude the live version counts as that read: Claude merges its changes into that version and publishes the result, and never resends the refused content unchanged. Claude omits `url` for a new artifact or to redeploy a file this conversation already published. For read, delete and the other calls that take a URL, it is the artifact to act on.

type_url.description: publish: the Artifact type to create this new, private Artifact from (a link from a 'types' listing). Claude omits `url`. Any `file_path`/`files` passed become the new Artifact's own files beside the type's fixed ones. read (no `url`): the type to describe. list: the type whose Artifacts to list, or Claude names the type with `type` instead.

auto_open.description: Only with `type_url` and no `file_path`: when the new Artifact opens for the person. Claude passes "after_first_write" when it will fill the Artifact right after creating it with a files publish to its url, so the person does not first see it empty. The Artifact then opens on that first write. Otherwise Claude omits it, and the Artifact opens when created; Claude always omits it for a type whose content it writes through a connector, such as a Claude Docs document, since no publish or store write follows to open it.

prompt.description: read, for an artifact shared with the person: what Claude needs from it, which steers the isolated summary.

force.description: publish: a last-resort overwrite that **discards** the newer published version. On a conflict, Claude merges its changes onto the newer content that the rejection hands it and publishes again. Claude passes true only when the person explicitly said to discard that specific version, and the server may still refuse it over a version saved from inside the page.

out_dir.description: read with `path`: the directory to save into. The default is this artifact's folder in Claude's scratchpad directory, where saving needs no approval. A published file lands at <out_dir>/<published path>, and saving it outside that default folder asks the person first. An asset's file is named by its id plus its type's extension; saving it outside the default folder is an ordinary file save the person may be asked to approve.

path.description: read: the file's published path inside the artifact, exactly as a 'files' listing printed it ("index.html" is the page itself). The file is saved locally, the result says where, and a small text file's contents are included. It can instead be an uploaded asset's id (32 hex characters, from an 'assets' listing or an upload result), and that asset is saved to a local file. delete: the id of the one asset to remove.

paths.description: read: several published paths in place of `path`, up to 256 in one call. Each file is saved as a single `path` would be, and the result lists where each one landed, or why it could not be read, with small text files' contents included while they fit.

after.description: list with scope 'assets' only: the `next` value from a previous listing, passed to continue it.

page.description: read only: true returns the rendered page in cases where a read otherwise returns something else. A typed Artifact's read leaves out the type's own page.

capabilities.description: publish: the runtime capabilities this page declares, as {name: config}. Claude loads the `artifact-capabilities` skill before passing it. On a redeploy Claude omits the field to keep what the page has, and {} clears it.

contract.description: publish: the artifact's runtime version. Leaving it out keeps the current version (the default), 'latest' upgrades, and an exact version pins or rolls back. It changes how the published page behaves, so Claude passes it only when the author explicitly intends that change.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. You will be notified when it exits — do not poll its output file while waiting. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- Do not commit files that likely contain secrets (.env, credentials.json, .claude/settings.local.json, etc). Warn the user if they specifically request to commit those files.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background.

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false)

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a listing from the system with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in a message from the system. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. # tabula

Small tools for CSV tables, standard library only (Python 3.9 or newer).

    tabula [--format text|csv|json] [--kind inner|left] [--keep first|last] COMMAND ARGS...

Commands (`docs/commands.md` describes them, `docs/transforms.md` the transforms):

- `show FILE` prints the whole table.
- `head FILE N` prints the first N rows.
- `cols FILE` lists the columns.
- `apply FILE COLUMN TRANSFORM...` runs transforms over one column.
- `sort FILE KEY...` orders the rows by one or more keys, each `COLUMN[:num][:desc]`.
- `filter FILE CONDITION...` keeps the rows where every condition `COLUMN OP VALUE` holds (`==`, `!=`, `>=`, `<=`, `>`, `<`, `~`).
- `group FILE BY AGGREGATE...` prints one row per distinct BY value with `count`, `sum:C`, `min:C`, `max:C` or `mean:C` columns.

Everything lives in `tabula/engine.py`: the table model, the transforms, the output formats and the commands.
A command is a function `cmd_NAME(args, opts)` returning a `Table`, registered in `COMMANDS`.
Mistakes in a file or a request exit 1 with `tabula: <message>` on stderr; a badly shaped command line exits 2.

1	"""tabula.engine -- the table model, the transforms, the output formats and the command line.
2	
3	This is the one module every command lives in. A command is a function `cmd_NAME(args, opts)` that gets the
4	positional arguments (a list of strings) and the options (a dict) and returns a Table, which `main` then prints in the
5	format asked for (`--format text|csv|json`, text by default). A mistake in a file or in a request raises TabulaError
6	(exit status 1); a command line that is not shaped right raises UsageError (exit status 2).
7	"""
8	import csv
9	import io
10	import json
11	import os
12	import re
13	import sys
14	import unicodedata
15	from decimal import (Context, Decimal, InvalidOperation, ROUND_HALF_UP, ROUND_FLOOR, ROUND_CEILING, ROUND_DOWN,
16	                     MAX_EMAX, MAX_PREC, MIN_EMIN, getcontext, localcontext)
17	from fractions import Fraction
18	
19	from .errors import TabulaError, UsageError
20	
21	PROG = "tabula"
22	FORMATS = ("text", "csv", "json")
23	# The choice options every command line accepts: name -> allowed values; the first-listed default is in DEFAULTS.
24	CHOICES = {"format": FORMATS, "kind": ("inner", "left"), "keep": ("first", "last")}
25	DEFAULTS = {"format": "text", "kind": "inner", "keep": "first"}
26	getcontext().prec = 60
27	# A context in which + - and comparisons on Decimals lose no digit, however long the numbers are.
28	EXACT = Context(prec=MAX_PREC, Emax=MAX_EMAX, Emin=MIN_EMIN)
29	
30	NUMBER = re.compile(r"[+-]?(?:\d+(?:\.\d*)?|\.\d+)")
31	
32	
33	# --- numbers -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
34	
35	def to_decimal(text):
36	    """The Decimal a cell holds, or None when it is not a plain decimal number (no exponent, no thousands marks)."""
37	    text = text.strip()
38	    if not NUMBER.fullmatch(text):
39	        return None
40	    try:
41	        return Decimal(text)
42	    except InvalidOperation:
43	        return None
44	
45	
46	def fmt_decimal(number):
47	    """A Decimal as plain text: no exponent, no negative zero."""
48	    text = format(number, "f")
49	    if text.startswith("-") and not text.strip("-0."):
50	        text = text[1:]
51	    return text
52	
53	
54	def fmt_2dp(value):
55	    """An int, Decimal or Fraction rounded half up (away from zero on a tie) to two decimals, always printed with two.
56	
57	    Exact for any size: it works on the value as a fraction, never through the context's precision."""
58	    scaled = Fraction(value) * 100
59	    whole = int((abs(scaled) + Fraction(1, 2)) // 1)
60	    number = EXACT.create_decimal(whole).scaleb(-2, EXACT)
61	    return format(number.copy_negate() if scaled < 0 and whole else number, "f")
62	
63	
64	def _need_number(value):
65	    number = to_decimal(value)
66	    if number is None:
67	        raise TabulaError("%r is not a number" % value)
68	    return number
69	
70	
71	def _need_cell_number(table, row_number, column, value):
72	    """The Decimal in a cell that must be a number; the mistake names the file, the data row (from 1) and the column."""
73	    try:
74	        return _need_number(value)
75	    except TabulaError as exc:
76	        raise TabulaError("%s: row %d: column %r: %s" % (table.source, row_number, column, exc))
77	
78	
79	def _need_count(arg, name):
80	    if arg is None or not arg.isdigit():
81	        raise TabulaError("%s needs a whole number argument, got %r" % (name, arg))
82	    return int(arg)
83	
84	
85	def _need_decimal_arg(arg, name):
86	    number = None if arg is None else to_decimal(arg)
87	    if number is None:
88	        raise TabulaError("%s needs a number argument, got %r" % (name, arg))
89	    return number
90	
91	
92	def _no_arg(name, arg):
93	    if arg is not None:
94	        raise TabulaError("%s takes no argument, got %r" % (name, arg))
95	
96	
97	def _need_text(arg, name):
98	    if arg is None:
99	        raise TabulaError("%s needs an argument" % name)
100	    return arg
101	
102	
103	# --- the table -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
104	
105	class Table:
106	    """Column names and rows of strings. `source` names where it came from, for messages."""
107	
108	    def __init__(self, columns, rows, source="<table>"):
109	        self.columns = list(columns)
110	        self.rows = [list(r) for r in rows]
111	        self.source = source
112	
113	    def __len__(self):
114	        return len(self.rows)
115	
116	    def index(self, name):
117	        """Position of a column; TabulaError when there is none."""
118	        try:
119	            return self.columns.index(name)
120	        except ValueError:
121	            raise TabulaError("%s: no column %r (columns: %s)" % (self.source, name, ", ".join(self.columns)))
122	
123	    def column(self, name):
124	        at = self.index(name)
125	        return [row[at] for row in self.rows]
126	
127	    def dicts(self):
128	        return [dict(zip(self.columns, row)) for row in self.rows]
129	
130	    def with_rows(self, rows, columns=None):
131	        return Table(self.columns if columns is None else columns, rows, self.source)
132	
133	
134	def parse_text(text, source):
135	    """CSV text into a Table. Blank lines are ignored; every row must have as many fields as the header."""
136	    if text.startswith("﻿"):
137	        text = text[1:]
138	    reader = csv.reader(io.StringIO(text, newline=""))
139	    columns, rows = None, []
140	    try:
141	        for fields in reader:
142	            if not fields:
143	                continue
144	            if columns is None:
145	                for name in fields:
146	                    if not name.strip():
147	                        raise TabulaError("%s: line %d: empty column name" % (source, reader.line_num))
148	                if len(set(fields)) != len(fields):
149	                    raise TabulaError("%s: line %d: duplicate column name" % (source, reader.line_num))
150	                columns = fields
151	                continue
152	            if len(fields) != len(columns):
153	                raise TabulaError("%s: line %d: expected %d fields, found %d"
154	                                  % (source, reader.line_num, len(columns), len(fields)))
155	            rows.append(fields)
156	    except csv.Error as exc:
157	        raise TabulaError("%s: line %d: %s" % (source, reader.line_num, exc))
158	    if columns is None:
159	        raise TabulaError("%s: no header line" % source)
160	    return Table(columns, rows, source)
161	
162	
163	def load(path):
164	    """Read a CSV file (UTF-8, optional byte order mark, LF or CRLF) into a Table."""
165	    try:
166	        with open(path, "rb") as fh:
167	            raw = fh.read()
168	    except OSError as exc:
169	        raise TabulaError("%s: cannot read: %s" % (path, exc.strerror or exc))
170	    try:
171	        text = raw.decode("utf-8")
172	    except UnicodeDecodeError:
173	        raise TabulaError("%s: not valid UTF-8" % path)
174	    return parse_text(text, path)
175	
176	
177	# --- output --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
178	
179	def render_text(table):
180	    cells = [table.columns] + table.rows
181	    widths = [max(len(row[i]) for row in cells) for i in range(len(table.columns))]
182	    lines = ["  ".join(cell.ljust(width) for cell, width in zip(row, widths)).rstrip() for row in cells]
183	    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
184	
185	
186	def render_csv(table):
187	    out = io.StringIO()
188	    writer = csv.writer(out, lineterminator="\n")
189	    writer.writerow(table.columns)
190	    writer.writerows(table.rows)
191	    return out.getvalue()
192	
193	
194	def render_json(table):
195	    return json.dumps(table.dicts(), ensure_ascii=False) + "\n"
196	
197	
198	RENDERERS = {"text": render_text, "csv": render_csv, "json": render_json}
199	
200	
201	def render(table, fmt="text"):
202	    return RENDERERS[fmt](table)
203	
204	
205	# --- transforms: one small function each, `name` or `name:ARG` in `apply` ----------------------------------------
206	
207	
208	def t_upper(value, arg=None):
209	    """The value in upper case.
210	
211	    Example: upper applied to '  Héllo, World 42 "x" ' gives '  HÉLLO, WORLD 42 "X" '.
212	    An argument that is missing or of the wrong kind is a TabulaError, not a guess.
213	    """
214	    _no_arg("upper", arg)
215	    return value.upper()
216	
217	
218	def t_lower(value, arg=None):
219	    """The value in lower case.
220	
221	    Example: lower applied to '  Héllo, World 42 "x" ' gives '  héllo, world 42 "x" '.
222	    An argument that is missing or of the wrong kind is a TabulaError, not a guess.
223	    """
224	    _no_arg("lower", arg)
225	    return value.lower()
226	
227	
228	def t_title(value, arg=None):
229	    """Each word capitalised.
230	
231	    Example: title applied to '  Héllo, World 42 "x" ' gives '  Héllo, World 42 "X" '.
232	    An argument that is missing or of the wrong kind is a TabulaError, not a guess.
233	    """
234	    _no_arg("title", arg)
235	    return value.title()
236	
237	
238	def t_capitalize(value, arg=None):
239	    """The first letter upper, the rest lower.
240	
241	    Example: capitalize applied to '  Héllo, World 42 "x" ' gives '  héllo, world 42 "x" '.
242	    An argument that is missing or of the wrong kind is a TabulaError, not a guess.
243	    """
244	    _no_arg("capitalize", arg)
245	    return value.capitalize()
246	
247	
248	def t_swapcase(value, arg=None):
249	    """Upper and lower case swapped.
250	
251	    Example: swapcase applied to '  Héllo, World 42 "x" ' gives '  hÉLLO, wORLD 42 "X" '.
252	    An argument that is missing or of the wrong kind is a TabulaError, not a guess.
253	    """
254	    _no_arg("swapcase", arg)
255	    return value.swapcase()
256	
257	
258	def t_strip(value, arg=None):
259	    """Without leading and trailing whitespace.
260	
261	    Example: strip applied to '  Héllo, World 42 "x" ' gives 'Héllo, World 42 "x"'.
262	    An argument that is missing or of the wrong kind is a TabulaError, not a guess.
263	    """
264	    _no_arg("strip", arg)
265	    return value.strip()
266	
267	
268	def t_lstrip(value, arg=None):
269	    """Without leading whitespace.
270	
271	    Example: lstrip applied to '  Héllo, World 42 "x" ' gives 'Héllo, World 42 "x" '.
272	    An argument that is missing or of the wrong kind is a TabulaError, not a guess.
273	    """
274	    _no_arg("lstrip", arg)
275	    return value.lstrip()
276	
277	
278	def t_rstrip(value, arg=None):
279	    """Without trailing whitespace.
280	
281	    Example: rstrip applied to '  Héllo, World 42 "x" ' gives '  Héllo, World 42 "x"'.
282	    An argument that is missing or of the wrong kind is a TabulaError, not a guess.
283	    """
284	    _no_arg("rstrip", arg)
285	    return value.rstrip()
286	
287	
288	def t_reverse(value, arg=None):
289	    """The characters in reverse order.
290	
291	    Example: reverse applied to '  Héllo, World 42 "x" ' gives ' "x" 24 dlroW ,olléH  '.
292	    An argument that is missing or of the wrong kind is a TabulaError, not a guess.
293	    """
294	    _no_arg("reverse", arg)
295	    return value[::-1]
296	
297	
298	def t_squeeze(value, arg=None):
299	    """Runs of whitespace collapsed to one space.
300	
301	    Example: squeeze applied to '  Héllo, World 42 "x" ' gives 'Héllo, World 42 "x"'.
302	    An argument that is missing or of the wrong kind is a TabulaError, not a guess.
303	    """
304	    _no_arg("squeeze", arg)
305	    return ' '.join(value.split())
306	
307	
308	def t_nospace(value, arg=None):
309	    """All whitespace removed.
310	
311	    Example: nospace applied to '  Héllo, World 42 "x" ' gives 'Héllo,World42"x"'.
312	    An argument that is missing or of the wrong kind is a TabulaError, not a guess.
313	    """
314	    _no_arg("nospace", arg)
315	    return ''.join(value.split())
316	
317	
318	def t_digits(value, arg=None):
319	    """Only the digits.
320	
321	    Example: digits applied to '  Héllo, World 42 "x" ' gives '42'.
322	    An argument that is missing or of the wrong kind is a TabulaError, not a guess.
323	    """
324	    _no_arg("digits", arg)
325	    return ''.join(c for c in value if c.isdigit())
326	
327	
328	def t_letters(value, arg=None):
329	    """Only the letters.
330	
331	    Example: letters applied to '  Héllo, World 42 "x" ' gives 'HélloWorldx'.
332	    An argument that is missing or of the wrong kind is a TabulaError, not a guess.
333	    """
334	    _no_arg("letters", arg)
335	    return ''.join(c for c in value if c.isalpha())
336	
337	
338	def t_alnum(value, arg=None):
339	    """Only letters and digits.
340	
341	    Example: alnum applied to '  Héllo, World 42 "x" ' gives 'HélloWorld42x'.
342	    An argument that is missing or of the wrong kind is a TabulaError, not a guess.
343	    """
344	    _no_arg("alnum", arg)
345	    return ''.join(c for c in value if c.isalnum())
346	
347	
348	def t_punct_free(value, arg=None):
349	    """Punctuation removed.
350	
351	    Example: punct_free applied to '  Héllo, World 42 "x" ' gives '  Héllo World 42 x '.
352	    An argument that is missing or of the wrong kind is a TabulaError, not a guess.
353	    """
354	    _no_arg("punct_free", arg)
355	    return re.sub(r'[^\w\s]', '', value)
356	
357	
358	def t_slug(value, arg=None):
359	    """Lower case words joined by dashes.
360	
361	    Example: slug applied to '  Héllo, World 42 "x" ' gives 'h-llo-world-42-x'.
362	    An argument that is missing or of the wrong kind is a TabulaError, not a guess.
363	    """
364	    _no_arg("slug", arg)
365	    return re.sub(r'[^a-z0-9]+', '-', value.lower()).strip('-')
366	
367	
368	def t_snake(value, arg=None):
369	    """Lower case words joined by underscores.
370	
371	    Example: snake applied to '  Héllo, World 42 "x" ' gives 'h_llo_world_42_x'.
372	    An argument that is missing or of the wrong kind is a TabulaError, not a guess.
373	    """
374	    _no_arg("snake", arg)
375	    return re.sub(r'[^a-z0-9]+', '_', value.lower()).strip('_')
376	
377	
378	def t_kebab(value, arg=None):
379	    """Lower case words joined by dashes (same as slug).
380	
381	    Example: kebab applied to '  Héllo, World 42 "x" ' gives 'h-llo-world-42-x'.
382	    An argument that is missing or of the wrong kind is a TabulaError, not a guess.
383	    """
384	    _no_arg("kebab", arg)
385	    return re.sub(r'[^a-z0-9]+', '-', value.lower()).strip('-')
386	
387	
388	def t_camel(value, arg=None):
389	    """Words run together, each capitalised.
390	
391	    Example: camel applied to '  Héllo, World 42 "x" ' gives 'HLloWorld42X'.
392	    An argument that is missing or of the wrong kind is a TabulaError, not a guess.
393	    """
394	    _no_arg("camel", arg)
395	    return ''.join(w.capitalize() for w in re.split(r'[^A-Za-z0-9]+', value) if w)
396	
397	
398	def t_initials(value, arg=None):
399	    """The first letter of each word, upper case.
400	
401	    Example: initials applied to '  Héllo, World 42 "x" ' gives 'HW4"'.
402	    An argument that is missing or of the wrong kind is a TabulaError, not a guess.
403	    """
404	    _no_arg("initials", arg)
405	    return ''.join(w[0].upper() for w in value.split())
406	
407	
408	def t_first_word(value, arg=None):
409	    """The first word.
410	
411	    Example: first_word applied to '  Héllo, World 42 "x" ' gives 'Héllo,'.
412	    An argument that is missing or of the wrong kind is a TabulaError, not a guess.
413	    """
414	    _no_arg("first_word", arg)

417

419	    """The last word.
420	
421	    Example: last_word applied to '  Héllo, World 42 "x" ' gives '"x"'.
422	    An argument that is missing or of the wrong kind is a TabulaError, not a guess.
423	    """

1457	def _parse_condition(spec):
1458	    """`COLUMN OP VALUE` into (column, operator, value): the leftmost operator wins, the longer one at the same spot."""
1459	    best = None
1460	    for op in FILTER_OPERATORS:
1461	        at = spec.find(op)
1462	        if at >= 0 and (best is None or at < best[0] or (at == best[0] and len(op) > len(best[1]))):
1463	            best = (at, op)
1464	    if best is None:
1465	        raise UsageError("filter: no operator in condition %r" % spec)
1466	    at, op = best
1467	    if at == 0:
1468	        raise UsageError("filter: no column name in condition %r" % spec)
1469	    return spec[:at], op, spec[at + len(op):]

1472	def _condition_holds(cell, op, value):
1473	    if op == "~":
1474	        return value.lower() in cell.lower()
1475	    left, right = to_decimal(cell), to_decimal(value)
1476	    if left is None or right is None:
1477	        left, right = cell, value
1478	    return {"==": left == right, "!=": left != right, ">=": left >= right,
1479	            "<=": left <= right, ">": left > right, "<": left < right}[op]

1495	def _parse_aggregate(spec):
1496	    """`count` or `KIND:COLUMN` (KIND one of sum, min, max, mean) into (kind, column or None)."""
1497	    kind, colon, column = spec.partition(":")

1500	    if kind not in GROUP_AGGREGATES or not colon or not column:
1501	        raise UsageError("group: %r is not an aggregate (count, sum:COLUMN, min:COLUMN, max:COLUMN or mean:COLUMN)" % spec)

1505	def _aggregate_value(kind, numbers, count):
1506	    if kind == "count":
1507	        return str(count)
1508	    if kind == "min":
1509	        return fmt_decimal(min(numbers))
1510	    if kind == "max":
1511	        return fmt_decimal(max(numbers))
1512	    total = sum(numbers, Decimal(0))
1513	    return fmt_decimal(total) if kind == "sum" else fmt_2dp(Fraction(total) / count)

1516	def cmd_group(args, opts):
1517	    _need_min_args(args, 3, "group FILE BY AGGREGATE...")
1518	    specs = args[2:]
1519	    if len(set(specs)) != len(specs):
1520	        raise UsageError("group: aggregate given twice in %s" % " ".join(specs))
1521	    aggregates = [_parse_aggregate(spec) for spec in specs]
1522	    table = load(args[0])
1523	    by_at = table.index(args[1])
1524	    positions = [None if column is None else table.index(column) for _, column in aggregates]
1525	    names = [spec.replace(":", "_") for spec in specs]
1526	    columns = [args[1]] + names
1527	    for at, name in enumerate(columns):
1528	        if name in columns[:at]:
1529	            raise TabulaError("%s: the result would have the column %r twice" % (table.source, name))
1530	    groups = {}
1531	    with localcontext(EXACT):
1532	        for number, row in enumerate(table.rows, 1):
1533	            members = groups.setdefault(row[by_at], [0] + [[] for _ in aggregates])
1534	            members[0] += 1
1535	            for k, ((_, column), at) in enumerate(zip(aggregates, positions), 1):
1536	                if at is not None:
1537	                    members[k].append(_need_cell_number(table, number, column, row[at]))
1538	        rows = [[key] + [_aggregate_value(kind, members[k], members[0]) for k, (kind, _) in enumerate(aggregates, 1)]
1539	                for key, members in groups.items()]
1540	    return Table(columns, rows, table.source)

1564	def parse_args(argv):
1565	    """(command, positional arguments, options) from the command line."""
1566	    opts, rest, i = dict(DEFAULTS), [], 0
1567	    while i < len(argv):
1568	        arg = argv[i]
1569	        if arg == "--":
1570	            rest.extend(argv[i + 1:])
1571	            break
1572	        name = arg[2:].split("=", 1)[0] if arg.startswith("--") else None
1573	        if arg in ("-h", "--help"):
1574	            opts["help"] = True

5-## Solution

Add two choice options, `--kind inner|left` (read by `join`) and `--keep first|last` (read by `dedupe`). Both are accepted on any command line, before or after the command, as `--opt value` or `--opt=value`. Each command gets its own test file `tests/test_COMMAND.py`, a section in `docs/commands.md` and a line in the README command list.
8-

Each one can be built, tested and merged on its own. The shared helpers listed below are added by **whichever child lands first that needs them**. Later children rebase and reuse them instead of writing their own.

11-## User Stories
12-
13-1. As a CSV user, I want `tabula sort FILE KEY...` (keys `col`, `col:num`, `col:desc`, `col:num:desc`/`col:desc:num`), so I can order rows stably by several keys.
14-2. As a CSV user, I want `tabula filter FILE CONDITION...` (`==`, `!=`, `>=`, `<=`, `>`, `<`, `~`), so I can keep only the rows where every condition holds.
15-3. As a CSV user, I want `tabula group FILE BY AGGREGATE...` (`count`, `sum:C`, `min:C`, `max:C`, `mean:C`), so I can summarise per distinct value.
16:4. As a CSV user, I want `tabula join LEFT RIGHT KEY [--kind inner|left]`, so I can combine two files.
17-5. As a CSV user, I want `tabula pivot FILE ROW COLUMN VALUE`, so I can turn the values of one column into columns of sums.
18-6. As a CSV user, I want `tabula dedupe FILE KEY... [--keep first|last]`, so I can drop duplicate rows.
19-7. As a CSV user, I want `tabula stats FILE COLUMN...`, so I can see count/min/max/mean/median per column.
20-8. As the maintainer, I want the four existing commands, their output, their exit statuses, `pip install .` (the `tabula` script) and `import tabula` to keep working unchanged.

22-## Implementation Decisions
23-
24-All of these follow the Original request below, which outranks this section wherever they differ.
25-
26-### Shared conventions (finish the module's own before adding to them; never a second way)
27-- **Option reading.** `parse_args` hard-codes `--format`. The first child that needs `--kind` or `--keep` turns this into ONE table-driven loop over the choice options, `{"format": FORMATS, "kind": ("inner","left"), "keep": ("first","last")}`, with defaults `format=text, kind=inner, keep=first` placed in `opts`. Both spellings are handled by that one loop, and so are the "needs a value" and "must be one of" usage errors (exit 2). The existing `--format` messages and behaviour stay identical. 30-- **Row-numbered mistakes.** `cmd_apply` already prefixes `"%s: row %d: "`. Add ONE helper for a cell that must be a number, built on `_need_number`/`to_decimal` (not a new parser). Its message is exactly `FILE: row N: column 'price': 'abc' is not a number` (column and value via `%r`). Row N is the 1-based data row in file order, never the sorted order. sort, group, pivot and stats all use it.
31-- **Number printing.** `sum`/`min`/`max` and pivot cells print with the existing `fmt_decimal` (plain, no exponent, no `+`, trailing zeros kept: `10.50` stays `10.50`, `+5` prints `5`). 36-### Per command (decisions on points the brief leaves open)
37-- **sort:** a KEY is split on `:`. The first part is the column, and every later part must be `num` or `desc`. An unknown modifier, a modifier given twice, or an empty column name is a usage error. Stable multi-key sort; `:desc` keeps file order for ties. With `:num`, an empty cell is not a number (mistake).
38-- **filter:** the operator is found by scanning left to right; at each position try `==`, `!=`, `>=`, `<=`, then `>`, `<`, `~`. The first match wins, and the longest wins at the same position. An empty VALUE is allowed (`city==` matches empty cells; `name~` matches every row). For every operator except `~`: when both sides pass `to_decimal`, compare as Decimal, otherwise compare as text by code point. `~` lower-cases both sides the way the `icontains` transform does (`.lower()`). With no rows left, only the header is printed.
39-- **group:** output column names are `BY`, then each aggregate as written with `:`→`_`. An aggregate is not valid when its name is unknown (e.g. `count:x`, `median:q`), when `sum`/`min`/`max`/`mean` has no column or an empty column, or when the same aggregate is given twice; each of these is a usage error. An output column name equal to BY (e.g. BY is `count` and `count` is asked for) is a mistake (exit 1, `column 'count' would appear twice`). Empty cells in an aggregated column are not numbers (mistake). `min`/`max` print the Decimal through `fmt_decimal`; among equal values the first in file order wins.

43-- **stats:** output columns are `column,count,min,max,mean,median`, with one row per requested COLUMN in the order asked (a column asked twice prints twice). A cell that is empty or only whitespace is skipped; every other cell must be a number. With no numbers, the row is `COLUMN,0,,,,`. The median of an even count is the exact mean of the two middle values, then rounded.
44-

46-- `unittest` only (no new dependencies). Each command has `tests/test_COMMAND.py`, which tests the engine function and the CLI through `python -m tabula` in a temp dir, the way `CliTests` in `tests/test_engine.py` does. 47-- `tests/test_engine.py` keeps passing unchanged (a test may be added there for the generalised option loop).
48-- `python -m unittest discover tests` is green on every child's PR. `pip install .` into a fresh venv still provides `tabula` and `import tabula`.

51-- Changing the behaviour or output of `show`/`head`/`cols`/`apply`, or the transforms.
52-- New dependencies, floating-point arithmetic, any options beyond `--kind` and `--keep`, reading stdin.
53-- Bumping `__version__`, packaging changes.

58-- [ ] `group`: first-appearance order; columns BY + aggregates named with `:`→`_`; `count`, `sum`, `min`, `max` (plain numbers, `10.50` stays) and `mean` (half up, always 2 dp); non-number → the sort message; no aggregate, an unknown aggregate or a duplicate → exit 2.
59:- [ ] `join`: LEFT columns + RIGHT minus KEY, `_right` suffix, a name still duplicated → exit 1; inner (default) and `--kind left` row order as specified; not exactly 3 args → exit 2.
60-- [ ] `pivot`: ROW + distinct COLUMN values in first-appearance order; exact sums, `0` for missing pairs; ROW == COLUMN → exit 2; empty COLUMN value → `FILE: row N: column 'C': empty value`; a COLUMN value equal to the ROW name → exit 1; non-number VALUE → the sort message; not exactly 4 args → exit 2.
61-- [ ] `dedupe`: `--keep first` (default) / `--keep last`; survivors in file order; no KEY → exit 2.
62-- [ ] `stats`: `column,count,min,max,mean,median`, rows in the order asked; empty/whitespace cells skipped; 2 dp half up for mean/median, exact even median; no numbers → `COLUMN,0,,,,`; non-number → the sort message; no COLUMN → exit 2.

"""The group command: the engine function and the command line through `python -m tabula`."""
import os, subprocess, sys, tempfile, unittest

ROOT = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "..")

from tabula.errors import TabulaError, UsageError

FILES = {
    "g.csv": "city,qty,price\nOslo,10.50,1\nRome,5,2\nOslo,+2,3\nRome,5.5,4\nBergen,-1.25,5\n",
    "bad.csv": "city,qty\nOslo,1\nRome,x\nOslo,\n",
    "empty.csv": "city,qty\n",
    "names.csv": "count,sum_qty,qty\na,1,2\n",
    "dash.csv": "-b,qty\nx,2\n",
}

    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
        for k, v in FILES.items():

                fh.write(v)
        env = dict(os.environ, PYTHONPATH=ROOT)

`tabula sort FILE KEY...` prints the whole table with its rows ordered by the keys. The first key decides; each later key
only orders rows the keys before it leave tied. A KEY is `COLUMN`, `COLUMN:num`, `COLUMN:desc` or `COLUMN:num:desc`; the

also with `:desc`.

CONDITION is `COLUMN`, an operator and a `VALUE`, written as one argument: `price>=10`, `city==Oslo`, `name~ann`. The
operators are `==`, `!=`, `>=`, `<=`, `>`, `<` and `~`. The operator is the leftmost one in the argument; where two start at
the same place the longer wins, so `price>=10` reads as `>=` and not `>`. The VALUE is the rest of the argument and may be
empty (`note==` keeps the rows whose `note` is empty).

For every operator except `~`, a cell and a VALUE that are both numbers compare as numbers (`10>9` holds, `1.0==1` holds);
otherwise they compare as text, by code point. `~` holds when the cell contains the VALUE, case aside. When no row is left

nothing before the operator is a usage error (exit 2), reported before the file is read.

    "names.csv": "count,sum_qty,qty\na,1,2\n",
    "dash.csv": "-b,qty\nx,2\n",

        env = dict(os.environ, PYTHONPATH=ROOT)
        p = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "tabula"] + list(argv), cwd=d, env=env, capture_output=True, text=True)
        return p.returncode, p.stdout, p.stderr

36-### Per command (decisions on points the brief leaves open)
37-- **sort:** a KEY is split on `:`. The first part is the column, and every later part must be `num` or `desc`. An unknown modifier, a modifier given twice, or an empty column name is a usage error. Stable multi-key sort; `:desc` keeps file order for ties. With `:num`, an empty cell is not a number (mistake).
38-- **filter:** the operator is found by scanning left to right; at each position try `==`, `!=`, `>=`, `<=`, then `>`, `<`, `~`. The first match wins, and the longest wins at the same position. An empty VALUE is allowed (`city==` matches empty cells; `name~` matches every row). For every operator except `~`: when both sides pass `to_decimal`, compare as Decimal, otherwise compare as text by code point. `~` lower-cases both sides the way the `icontains` transform does (`.lower()`). With no rows left, only the header is printed.
39-- **group:** output column names are `BY`, then each aggregate as written with `:`→`_`. An aggregate is not valid when its name is unknown (e.g. `count:x`, `median:q`), when `sum`/`min`/`max`/`mean` has no column or an empty column, or when the same aggregate is given twice; each of these is a usage error. An output column name equal to BY (e.g. BY is `count` and `count` is asked for) is a mistake (exit 1, `column 'count' would appear twice`). Empty cells in an aggregated column are not numbers (mistake). `min`/`max` print the Decimal through `fmt_decimal`; among equal values the first in file order wins.
40:- **join:** KEY must exist in both files (exit 1 via `Table.index` naming the file). Columns: all LEFT columns, then RIGHT columns minus KEY, with `_right` appended when LEFT has the name. A name that still appears twice is a mistake (exit 1, the message names the column). Inner: for each LEFT row, one row per matching RIGHT row, in RIGHT order. Left: the same, plus unmatched LEFT rows once, with `""` in the RIGHT columns.
41-- **pivot:** ROW == COLUMN is a usage error. VALUE may be any column. An empty ROW value is a normal group. An empty COLUMN value → `FILE: row N: column 'C': empty value`. A COLUMN value equal to the ROW column's name is a mistake whose message names the file, the row, the column and the value. A pair that never occurs prints `0`.
42-- **dedupe:** text equality on the tuple of KEY values; `--keep first` (default) or `last`. The rows that remain keep file order.
43-- **stats:** output columns are `column,count,min,max,mean,median`, with one row per requested COLUMN in the order asked (a column asked twice prints twice). A cell that is empty or only whitespace is skipped; every other cell must be a number. With no numbers, the row is `COLUMN,0,,,,`. The median of an even count is the exact mean of the two middle values, then rounded.

## sort

`tabula sort FILE KEY...` prints the whole table with its rows ordered by the keys. The first key decides; each later key
only orders rows the keys before it leave tied. A KEY is `COLUMN`, `COLUMN:num`, `COLUMN:desc` or `COLUMN:num:desc`; the

With `:num` they compare as numbers. `:desc` puts the largest first. Rows that tie on every key keep their file order,

`tabula filter FILE CONDITION...` prints the header and the rows for which every CONDITION holds, in file order. A
CONDITION is `COLUMN`, an operator and a `VALUE`, written as one argument: `price>=10`, `city==Oslo`, `name~ann`. The
operators are `==`, `!=`, `>=`, `<=`, `>`, `<` and `~`. The operator is the leftmost one in the argument; where two start at
the same place the longer wins, so `price>=10` reads as `>=` and not `>`. The VALUE is the rest of the argument and may be
empty (`note==` keeps the rows whose `note` is empty).

"""The group command: the engine function and the command line through `python -m tabula`."""
import os, subprocess, sys, tempfile, unittest

ROOT = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "..")
sys.path.insert(0, ROOT)
from tabula import engine
from tabula.errors import TabulaError, UsageError

FILES = {
    "g.csv": "city,qty,price\nOslo,10.50,1\nRome,5,2\nOslo,+2,3\nRome,5.5,4\nBergen,-1.25,5\n",
    "bad.csv": "city,qty\nOslo,1\nRome,x\nOslo,\n",
    "empty.csv": "city,qty\n",
    "names.csv": "count,sum_qty,qty\na,1,2\n",
    "dash.csv": "-b,qty\nx,2\n",
}


def run_cli(*argv):
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
        for k, v in FILES.items():
            with open(os.path.join(d, k), "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as fh:
                fh.write(v)
        env = dict(os.environ, PYTHONPATH=ROOT)
        p = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "tabula"] + list(argv), cwd=d, env=env, capture_output=True, text=True)
        return p.returncode, p.stdout, p.stderr


def group_text(text, *args):
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
        path = os.path.join(d, "t.csv")
        with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as fh:
            fh.write(text)
        return engine.cmd_group([path] + list(args), dict(engine.DEFAULTS))

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in messages from the system in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork runs in the background and keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate. Subagents run in the background; you'll be notified when one completes. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort.
